title: Vitamins E and C in the prevention of cardiovascular disease in men: the Physicians' Health Study II randomized controlled trial
authors: Sesso HD, Buring JE, Christen WG, Kurth T, Belanger C, MacFadyen J, et al.
population: US male physicians aged 50 years or older, 754 (5.1%) with prevalent cardiovascular disease, in a 2x2x2x2 factorial trial of vitamin E, vitamin C, beta-carotene and a multivitamin
funder: Supported by NIH grants CA 97193, CA 34944, CA 40360, HL 26490 and HL 34595 and an investigator-initiated grant from BASF Corporation. BASF, Wyeth Pharmaceuticals and DSM Nutritional Products had no role in the study design; conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis and interpretation of the data; or preparation, review or approval of the manuscript.
inKindSupport: Study agents and packaging provided by BASF Corporation (vitamin C, vitamin E, beta-carotene), Wyeth Pharmaceuticals (multivitamin) and DSM Nutritional Products.
authorConflicts: Sesso reported investigator-initiated funding from Roche Vitamins (now DSM Nutritional Products) and others; Christen from DSM Nutritional Products (Roche); Kurth from Bayer, McNeil, Merck and Wyeth Consumer Healthcare; Manson assistance with study pills and packaging from BASF and Cognis; Buring study agents from Bayer Healthcare and the Natural Source Vitamin E Association; Glynn funding from Bristol-Myers Squibb and AstraZeneca; Gaziano funding from Veroscience and Amgen and consultancy or honoraria from Bayer and Pfizer.
result: Vitamin C 500 mg daily versus placebo, mean follow-up 8.0 years: major cardiovascular events in 619 of 7329 versus 626 of 7312 men (10.8 and 10.9 per 1000 person-years; HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.89 to 1.11); total mortality 857 versus 804 (HR 1.07, 0.97 to 1.18).
